draft.title: The Tet Offensive
card: In January 1968, during the Tet new year holiday, North Vietnamese forces and the Viet Cong attacked cities and towns across South Vietnam. Targets included Saigon, where fighters entered the grounds of the US embassy, and the city of Hue.

Militarily, the attacks failed. US and South Vietnamese troops drove the attackers back, and the communists lost very large numbers of fighters. The people of South Vietnam did not rise up to support them.
Politically, the effect was different. US leaders had told the public that the war was being won. Television and newspaper reports of fighting in Saigon made that claim look false.
Many Americans lost trust in their leaders and turned against the war. President Johnson later announced he would not seek re-election, and peace talks began.
draft.remember: Tet was a communist military defeat that still weakened American support for the war.

a.q: Why did the Tet Offensive turn many Americans against the war?
opts: It made official claims of progress look false
It destroyed most of the US forces in Vietnam
It led South Vietnam's people to join the communists
It showed that the communists had won every battle
a.why: Americans had been told the war was being won, and images of fighting in Saigon contradicted this. The attacks did not destroy US forces, because the communists were driven back with heavy losses.
a.clue: Think about what leaders had told the public before the attacks.

b.q: Which statement best describes the results of the Tet Offensive?
opts: A military failure for the communists but a US political blow
A military and political victory for the communists
A military victory for the US that lifted support at home
A military and political failure for the communists
b.why: The communists lost many fighters and gained no uprising, so the attacks failed militarily. Yet public trust in the US government fell and opposition grew, so the political effect hurt the US. Calling it a defeat in every sense ignores this.
b.clue: Judge the battlefield result and the effect on American opinion separately.
